clue.text: Politically favoured Dicky

parts.note: a policy or party favoured by the voters is popular
a dicky is a detachable false shirt-front worn under a dinner jacket

explanation.surface: A bare description of some well-liked item of evening wear, or of a politician in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: A dicky is a false shirt-front, so a 'politically favoured' one is a popular front, the name for a coalition of left-wing parties such as those of 1930s France and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition of left and centre parties formed to win power is known by this name, so it is literally a front the electorate favours.

clue.text: Choice feller tearing up the road.

definitions.text: Choice feller tearing up the road.

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the choice
an axe fells trees

explanation.surface: A fine fellow is digging up the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with a pointed iron head for breaking hard ground, used by road-menders.

clue.text: Sudden, pain a knife causes

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone notes the stabbing pain a blade inflicts.
explanation.walkthrough: A panga is a broad-bladed machete from East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This broad heavy blade, used in Africa for clearing bush, is a large cutting tool.

clue.text: Hardly Queen Victoria's view of your cadenza on a bugle, Hal

indicators.note: a cadenza is a free flourish improvised on a theme, so the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: A trumpeter is told the old Queen would not have enjoyed his showy solo.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is said to have remarked 'We are not amused', so her view was that a thing was hardly funny. 'cadenza on' rearranges ABUGLEHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria famously found things not amusing, so 'hardly' this means not at all funny in her eyes.

clue.text: Burlington House a shelter from it ?

definitions.text: Burlington House a shelter from it ?

parts.words: Burlington House a shelter from it ?
parts.note: the Royal Academy (RA) building as somewhere to go in out of the weather, so 'it' is the weather

explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House in Piccadilly houses the Royal Academy, RA; being IN there keeps off the wet, so RA + IN shadows the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter keeps off falling water, the thing one goes indoors to escape.

clue.text: Contemplated making a dredger

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone eyed a dredger under construction.
explanation.definitionFit: To have regarded something is to have looked at it thoughtfully, considered it.

clue.text: Midland tangles, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: knots are tangles

explanation.surface: Someone describes a knotted mess in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is the short form of Nottinghamshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottinghamshire, abbreviated, lies in the Midlands of England.

clue.text: Sprightly levitated lass

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman
something levitated floats on air

explanation.surface: A lively girl rises into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A deb is a debutante, a society girl making her first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair once meant cheerful and light of heart, close to lively and jaunty.

clue.text: Six-player Asian tests for a change

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: E stands for Eastern, so Asian

explanation.surface: A six-a-side Asian team plays some different test matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges E and TESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six musicians or the six-line close of a sonnet is this group of six.

clue.text: Against 'electricity failure causing-a mix-up

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
when a fuse blows, the lights go out; the circuit is said to be fusing

explanation.surface: A power cut throws a household into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bewildering causes a mix-up in the mind.

clue.text: That's the spot, say to soothe

definitions.meaning: pointing to a place: in that position
the word repeated as a comforting murmur

explanation.surface: Someone finds the sore place and murmurs comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb points to a place, as in 'put it over in that spot'; and 'there, there' is what one says to calm a child.

clue.text: A couldn't-care-less attitude, yes, about a right of way

indicators.note: the word for yes goes about, that is around, the right of way

parts.note: ay is an old and parliamentary word for yes
a public footpath is a right of way

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a dispute about a public footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference, a lack of interest or concern, is a couldn't-care-less attitude.

clue.text: Historian before Waverley ?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
Waverley was Sir Walter Scott's first novel, so it stands for its author

explanation.surface: A question about which writer came earlier than the Waverley novels.
explanation.walkthrough: William H. Prescott was an American historian of the conquest of Mexico and Peru. Waverley (1814) is Walter Scott's first novel, standing here for Scott himself.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hickling Prescott was a nineteenth-century American writer of history.

clue.text: Young Greek begins an epistle to a barmaid

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the epistle starts the word, coming before the barmaid

parts.note: Ep. is the standard abbreviation for Epistle, as in Bible references
Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods, so a classical barmaid

explanation.surface: A Greek youth writes his first letter to a woman who serves drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe poured the nectar for the gods on Olympus, hence the barmaid.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an ephebe was a youth of about eighteen entering military training and citizenship.

clue.text: When Ian toasts Jan

parts.note: a Scotsman (Ian) drinking to January, seeing in the new year

explanation.walkthrough: Ian is a typically Scottish name, and 'Jan' is January rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish New Year's Eve celebration, when the coming month of January is welcomed with drinks.

clue.text: One above corporal punishment ?

parts.note: read as a rank: the soldier who ranks above a corporal, with 'punishment' tagged on to make the phrase corporal punishment

explanation.definitionFit: In the army this rank sits immediately above corporal.

clue.text: Bobby Shaftoe's

parts.note: the opening line of the old song 'Bobby Shafto's ___, silver buckles on his knee'

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue is a fill-in-the-blank: 'Bobby Shaftoe's ----'. The folk song continues 'silver buckles on his knee'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk song the sweetheart Bobby Shafto has left to be a sailor.

clue.text: How readable was Jabberwocky?

parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass Alice can read the poem only by holding it to a looking-glass

explanation.definitionFit: The verses were printed in reverse, so they read correctly only as a reflection.

clue.text: Such was the attraction of mine

definitions.text: Such was the attraction of mine

parts.words: Such was the attraction of mine
parts.note: read 'mine' as a naval mine that is drawn to a ship's steel hull, rather than as the possessive

explanation.definitionFit: Some sea mines were set off by the magnetic field of a ship's steel hull, so their pull was of this kind.

clue.text: Like Hamlet's queen to whom a medico, gave out-of-date treatment

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
bleeding a patient was an old-fashioned remedy

explanation.surface: Hamlet's mother is let blood by an old-school doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet the Player speaks of 'the mobled queen', meaning muffled about the face.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Player's speech Hecuba is the 'mobled queen', her head wrapped up, so muffled.

clue.text: Discover

parts.note: read as dis-cover: take the covering off

explanation.definitionFit: To take the wrapping off a parcel is to uncover it, which is the old literal sense of 'discover'.

clue.text: Transformations by means of stringed instruments

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
ukes are ukuleles

explanation.surface: Some change is wrought by plucking strings.
explanation.walkthrough: A transformation is an old word for a hairpiece or wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformation was a wig or false hair worn to change one's look, and periwigs are wigs.

clue.text: Note the scaling devices used by Laputan flappers

definitions.note: the clue means the things used by these servants, a plural noun

parts.note: B is a musical note
ladders are used for scaling walls

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the climbing gear of a strange island's servants.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gulliver's Travels the people of Laputa are so lost in thought that servants called flappers strike their mouths and ears with inflated bladders to rouse them.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's flappers carried blown-up animal bladders on sticks to tap their masters awake.

clue.text: Evasive trick

parts.note: a plain description of a ruse to avoid something

explanation.definitionFit: A trick to slip out of something, such as a tax ploy, is a cunning way out.

clue.text: As day-before-yesterday's news is to yesterday's

definitions.text: As day-before-yesterday's news is to yesterday's

parts.words: As day-before-yesterday's news is to yesterday's
parts.note: an analogy: older news is less fresh than news a day younger

explanation.definitionFit: Older news is less fresh, so two-day-old news is more out of date than one-day-old news.

clue.text: Stop sailor, as George Washington did not his father

definitions.meaning: in sailing language, to stop a ship with its head to the wind

definitions.text: as George Washington did not his father
definitions.meaning: the tale that young Washington could not tell a falsehood about the cherry tree

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to halt, and a famous story of childhood honesty follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaving to is the seaman's way of halting; and in the legend Washington told his father the truth about felling the cherry tree.

clue.text: In Rome both were seen in a pulpit

definitions.meaning: an early Christian raised reading desk in a church

explanation.surface: Two Romans are seen preaching from a raised stand.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin it means the pair together; in church history it is the raised lectern from which scripture was read.

clue.text: Not found among west-country fauna

parts.note: a creature that does not live wild in the south-west of England, being African

explanation.definitionFit: This large antelope lives on the African plains, not in Devon or Cornwall.

clue.text: Dinner for Commonwealth Parliamentary beefeaters ?

parts.note: a meal of beef suited to members of the Rump, the Parliament of Cromwell's Commonwealth

explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament sat during the English Commonwealth (1648-53), so its members might dine on a cut called after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters is a fitting meal for beef-eaters who sat in the Rump.

clue.text: That the generations of Murphy fail not

definitions.text: That the generations of Murphy fail not

parts.words: That the generations of Murphy fail not
parts.note: 'Murphy' is slang for a spud, so the line reads as a prayer for the next crop of them

explanation.definitionFit: Tubers kept back and planted to grow next year's crop keep the line of spuds going.
